summary: Aroostook County lookout on Lawler Hill, listed under Benedicta: a 1914 report planned a steel tower for 1915; the register gives 1978 as its removal year.

facts.design: Steel tower; a volunteer list gives 48 feet and a build year of 1915
facts.status_note: Gone; the register gives 1978 as the removal year and no source describes what remains

events.note: A man kept for lookout purposes on Lawler Hill, per the 1914 Forest Commissioner's report
Volunteer list gives 1915 for a 48-foot steel tower; the 1914 report describes it as a plan for spring 1915

evidence.supports: fire towers spotted fires early to protect timber and paper industries
evidence.quote: It was especially important to spot fires quickly and get firefighting crews to the scene early to minimize damage and hence loss to the industries that depended on Maine's trees, especially lumber and papermaking.

evidence.supports: register lists the site under Benedicta, Aroostook County
1914 report: a man kept for lookout purposes on Lawler Hill; material on hand for a steel tower in spring 1915
evidence.quote: Have kept a man for lookout purposes on Lawler Hill at which place we already have the material with which to erect a steel tower in the spring of 1915.

evidence.supports: volunteer list: 1915 entry for a 48-foot steel tower, citing the 1914 Forest Commissioner's report
evidence.quote: 1915: A 48-foot steel tower constructed. (1914 Forest Commissioner's Report)

evidence.supports: association list: Lawler Hill tower listed as gone
evidence.quote: Lawler Hill Aroostook 45.76992 -68.43113 Tower Gone FFLOS US 116, ME 42

sources.title: Looking Out: Maine's Fire Towers
sources.publisher: Maine History Online, Maine Memory Network

sources.title: Lawler Hill Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Only the register gives a removal year (1978). The volunteer list is the only source for the 1915 build, and it cites the 1914 report, which describes a plan, so completion is not confirmed. No staffing beyond the 1914 mention, and no fire or access information was found. Coordinates from the FFA list (45.76992, -68.43113) were not checked against a second source. Two searches (neither confirmed the 1915 build or the 1978 removal) and about four page reads. No corrections proposed.
